title: 2D Mensuration
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for 2D Mensuration. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

coverage: Perimeter and area of plane figures

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Perimeter and area

Perimeter measures boundary length; area measures the region inside. Rectangle: (\(P=2(l+w)\)), (\(A=lw\)). Triangle: (\(A=1/2 bh\)). Parallelogram: (\(A=bh\)). Trapezium: (\(A=1/2(a+b)h\)), where (\(a,b\)) are parallel sides.

Circles and sectors

For radius (\(r\)), circumference is (\(2 \pi r\)) and area is (\(\pi r^2\)). An arc with central angle (theta) degrees has length (\((theta/360) \times 2 \pi r\)); its sector area is (\((theta/360) \times \pi r^2\)).

Composite regions and scale

Break a composite figure into known shapes or subtract a cut-out. A length scale factor (\(k\)) multiplies perimeter by (\(k\)) and area by (\(k^2\)). State whether a diagram's dimensions refer to a radius, diameter, height or slant side.

Worked example: A 14 cm by 10 cm rectangle has a 4 cm by 3 cm corner removed. The remaining area is (\(14 \times 10 - 4 \times 3=128 cm^2\)).

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Sketch and label dimensions before selecting a formula.
  • Convert every length to the same unit before finding area or perimeter.
  • For a shaded region, calculate the enclosing area and subtract unshaded parts.
  • Use the diameter as (\(2r\)) only when the problem supplies a diameter.
  • Check whether the requested boundary includes an internal edge around a cut-out.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• Square: (\(A=s^2\)), (\(P=4s\)); circle: (\(A=\pi r^2\)), circumference (\(2 \pi r\)).
  • Area uses square units and perimeter uses linear units.
  • Changing all lengths by factor (\(k\)) changes area by factor (\(k^2\)).
  • For an annulus, area is (\(\pi(R^2-r^2)\)).

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    A circle has radius 7 cm. Using (\(\pi=22/7\)), what is its area?

    1. (\(44\text{ cm}^2\))
    2. (\(154\text{ cm}^2\))
    3. (\(308\text{ cm}^2\))
    4. (\(49\text{ cm}^2\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(154\text{ cm}^2\))

    Area (\(=\pi r^2=(22/7)\cdot49=154\text{ cm}^2\)).

  2. Core:

    A rectangle is 8 cm by 5 cm. What is its perimeter?

    1. (\(13\text{ cm}\))
    2. (\(26\text{ cm}\))
    3. (\(40\text{ cm}\))
    4. (\(80\text{ cm}\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(26\text{ cm}\))

    Perimeter (\(=2(8+5)=26\text{ cm}\)).

  3. Foundation:

    Find the area of a triangle with base 12 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm.

    1. (\(19 cm^2\))
    2. (\(42 cm^2\))
    3. (\(84 cm^2\))
    4. (\(168 cm^2\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(42 cm^2\))

    Area is (\(1/2 \times 12 \times 7=42 cm^2\)).

  4. Standard:

    A circle has diameter 14 cm. Find its circumference in terms of (pi).

    1. (\(7 \pi cm\))
    2. (\(14 \pi cm\))
    3. (\(28 \pi cm\))
    4. (\(49 \pi cm\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(14 \pi cm\))

    Radius is 7 cm. Circumference is (\(2 \pi \times 7=14 \pi cm\)).

  5. Challenge:

    A square's side is increased by 20%. By what percentage does its area increase?

    1. (\(20%\))
    2. (\(40%\))
    3. (\(44%\))
    4. (\(144%\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(44%\))

    The new side factor is (\(1.2\)). Area factor is (\(1.2^2=1.44\)), so area increases by 44%.
